questions.q: How fast does the ISS fly, and how long does it take to go once round the Earth?
questions.do: Look at Speed and Once round Earth in Why 16 sunrises a day, with the height slider at 420 km.
questions.a: About 7.66 km every second (about 27,600 km/h) and about 92.8 minutes per lap. Lower orbits need to go faster; higher ones go slower.

questions.q: Why does the crew see about 16 sunrises a day, and can there be a day with no sunset at all?
questions.do: Press Play the day in A day aboard and watch the bottom band. Then move the Sun angle to the orbit slider to 75°.
questions.a: The station goes round Earth about 15½ times a day and passes through Earth's shadow once each lap, so it gets a sunrise roughly every 93 minutes. When the Sun angle is above about 70°, the station never enters the shadow and stays in sunshine all day.

questions.q: How much does the ISS sink each month because of air drag with an average Sun, and what happens when the Sun is stormy?
questions.do: In Falling slowly: drag and reboosts, press Average Sun, then Stormy Sun, and read Height lost per month and Reboost every.
questions.a: With an average Sun, about 2 km a month (about 70 m a day), so a reboost about every 4 weeks. A stormy Sun puffs up the upper air, so the station sinks about three times faster and needs reboosts much more often.

questions.q: For 7 people over 180 days, how much new drinking water must be launched with today's 98% recycling, compared with no recycling?
questions.do: In Air, water and food, set 7 people and 180 days, then press No recycling and Today: 98%.
questions.a: About 3,150 litres with no recycling, but only about 63 litres at 98%. That saves about 3 tonnes of launch weight. Food can't be recycled: about 2,268 kg must still be sent up.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian aboard the ISS, and on which mission and year?
questions.a: Shubhanshu Shukla, on Axiom-4. He launched on 25 June 2025, docked on 26 June, and returned on 15 July 2025, 41 years after Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space on the Soviet station Salyut 7 in 1984.
